Extra Gooey Cinnamon Rolls (Bakery-Style & No-Knead) Dough * 1 tsp yeast * 2 tbsp sugar * 343 g milk (about 1½ cups) * 480 g flour (about 4 cups + 2 tbsp) * 1 tsp salt * 60 g softened butter (about 4 tbsp) Filling * 140 g softened butter (10 tbsp) * 140 g brown sugar (about ⅔ cup) * 3½ tbsp ground cinnamon Butter Vanilla Frosting * 85 g softened butter (6 tbsp) * 180 g powdered sugar (about 1½ cups) * 1 tbsp vanilla extract Instructions 1. In a bowl, mix the yeast, sugar, and milk. Add the flour and mix until combined. Add the salt and softened butter, then stretch and fold (or coil fold) until the butter is fully incorporated. 2. Cover and let the dough rise for about 2 hours, or until doubled in size. 3. Roll the dough into a large rectangle. Spread the softened butter evenly over the dough, then sprinkle with the brown sugar and cinnamon. 4. Cut the dough into 6 long strips, then roll each strip into a cinnamon roll. 5. Sprinkle a little of the cinnamon sugar mixture into the bottom of the pan, then place the rolls on top. 6. Cover and let them rest for 15 minutes. 7. Mix a little milk with 1 tbsp melted butter, then spoon about 2 tbsp of the mixture over each cinnamon roll. 8. Bake at 350°F (175°C) for 25–30 minutes, or until golden brown. 9. As soon as they come out of the oven, cover them with a clean kitchen towel until warm. Then spread the frosting on top. That’s the key to extra-soft cinnamon rolls. #cinnamonrolls #cinnamonroll #baking #bread #breadtok

One bite and you’re hooked 🤤 Crispy Beef Cones (12 cones) Ingredients For the cones:  • 6 tortillas (25–30 cm / 10–12 inches)  • Toothpicks For the topping:  • Mozzarella cheese, 100 g  • Chopped parsley, 1 tsp For the beef mixture:  • Ground beef, 400 g(0.8lb)   • 1 yellow onion, finely chopped  • Garlic, 4 cloves, minced  • Red bell pepper, diced (about 1 small)  • Green bell pepper, diced (about 1 small)  • Tomato paste, 1 big tbsp   • Soy milk, 100 ml (~ ½ cup) Seasoning:  • Paprika, 1 tbsp  • Chili powder, 1 tsp  • Turmeric, 1 tsp  • Garlic powder, 1 tsp  • Black pepper, 1 tsp  • Garam masala, 1 tsp  • Salt, ½ tsp Instructions 1.⁠ ⁠Prepare the beef mixture:  • Heat a little oil in a pan over medium heat. Add the onion and sauté until soft.  • Add the minced garlic and cook 30 seconds until fragrant.  • Add the ground beef and cook until browned, breaking it apart as it cooks.  • Stir in tomato paste, soy milk, diced bell peppers, and all seasonings. Cook until slightly thickened. Remove from heat and let cool slightly. 2.⁠ ⁠Prepare the cones:  • Cut tortillas in half. Roll each half into a cone shape and secure the edge with a toothpick. Baking Method:  1. Preheat oven to 190°C (375°F).  2. Place cones on a baking tray lined with parchment paper. Lightly spray with cooking spray.  3. Bake for 10–12 minutes until crispy and golden.  4. Fill each cone with the beef mixture and top with mozzarella cheese.  5. Return to oven for 5 minutes until cheese melts.  6. Garnish with parsley and serve warm. Air Fryer Method:   1. Preheat air fryer to 180°C (356°F).  2. Lightly spray cones with cooking spray and place them in the air fryer basket. Strawberry Nutella Brownies 🍓🤎 Perfect brownies for summer!  (recipe makes an 8x8 pan) Ingredients:  10 tbsp (140g) unsalted butter, melted 1 cup (200g) granulated sugar ¼ cup (50g) brown sugar, packed  2 eggs, room temp 1 tsp vanilla extract ½ cup + 2 tbsp (56g) unsweetened cocoa powder ½ tsp salt 1 tbsp (13g) vegetable oil ½ cup (63g) all purpose flour, spooned & leveled or weighed (don’t pack it in) ¾ cup chocolate chips 190g (~⅔ cup) Nutella  Topping: Strawberry slices, patted dry (as many as you want/enough to cover the top) Nutella (to spread over the top & drizzle)  Instructions: Line an 8x8 pan with parchment paper. Spread the nutella onto the parchment into a thin, even square the size of the pan. Freeze for at least 30 minutes or until frozen solid. Preheat oven to 325°F and line/grease an 8x8 pan with parchment. In a large bowl, whisk melted butter, granulated sugar, and brown sugar until smooth. Add eggs and vanilla, then whisk vigorously for 1-2 minutes. Stir in cocoa powder and salt until fully combined. Mix in oil, then gently fold in the flour until just combined (don’t over mix). Fold in chocolate chips. Spread half the batter into the greased pan. Place the frozen nutella sheet on top of it. Then, spread the remaining batter over it to cover the nutella layer completely. Bake for 35-40 minutes, or until a toothpick near the center comes out with no wet batter. It should just come out with a little nutella & slightly moist crumbs. Let the brownies cool completely. Spread a thin layer of nutella over the cooled brownies, add strawberry slices (patted dry) all over the top, and drizzle with more nutella.  Best enjoyed fresh!  #bakingrecipe #brownies #chocolatestrawberries #nutella #recipe

Brown Butter Chocolate Chip Banana Bread 🍌 For all of you asking about the app, search “Osta Recipes” on the app or Google play store ‼️🫶 I have tested over 100 banana bread recipes and after countless adjustments, these officially have claimed the #1 spot 👑 Ingredients -3 ripe bananas (brown spots = flavor) -9 tbsp unsalted butter (browns down to ~½ cup) -1 large egg, room temp -¾ cup brown sugar -¼ cup white sugar -1½ cups all-purpose flour -1 tsp baking soda -½ tsp baking powder -½ tsp salt -1 tsp cinnamon -1 tsp vanilla extract or paste -1 to 1½ cups semi-sweet chocolate chips (measure with your heart) Instructions: 1. Add butter to a saucepan over medium heat. Stir often. It’ll melt, foam, sizzle, then turn golden with a nutty smell. Once browned (do not burn), pour into a  bowl and place in the freezer for 5 mins. You want it warm, not hot. 2. In a large bowl, mash bananas until mostly smooth. Add 1/2 cup of the browned butter, brown sugar, white sugar, egg, and vanilla. Whisk for 1 to 2 mins until glossy. 3. Add flour, baking soda, baking powder, salt, and cinnamon. You can mix these in a separate bowl first, or be lazy like me and add them straight in. Just mix very thoroughly so everything is evenly distributed. 4. Preheat to 350°F / 175°C. Once no dry flour remains, fold in about 1 cup of chocolate chips. Save the rest for topping. 5. Line or grease a loaf pan and pour in the batter. Sprinkle remaining chocolate chips on top. Bake for 60 mins, loosely covering with foil halfway through to prevent over-browning. 6. Insert a toothpick into the center. It should come out with a few moist crumbs, not wet batter. MARRY ME MASH 🥔✨ Recipe below ⬇️ This is the ultimate recipe for luxurious mashed potato. Ultra-smooth, buttery, garlic-thyme infused, finished with white pepper and nutmeg. Make no mistake - this is pure indulgence, and it will make your guests so silent at the table. Marry Me Mash: Peel and cube 1kg Maris Piper potatoes. Add to cold salted water, bring to the boil, then simmer gently until completely tender. Drain and leave to steam dry for 20-30 minutes (this step is key for texture). Meanwhile, gently simmer 200ml whole milk and 200ml double cream with 4 chopped garlic cloves and 3-4 thyme sprigs for 30 minutes to infuse. Strain and keep warm. Pass the dried potatoes through a ricer, then fold through 150g melted butter. For extra smoothness, push through a fine mesh sieve. Add the warm infused cream one ladle at a time until silky and smooth but still holding its shape. Season with fine salt, white pepper and a small grating of nutmeg. Taste and adjust. Bonus recipe - Braised Short Rib (perfect with this mash): Season 3-4 large beef short ribs generously with salt and pepper and sear in a hot casserole pot with 1 tbsp oil until deeply browned. Remove. In the same pot soften 1 diced onion, 2 diced celery sticks and 2 diced carrots. Add 2 tbsp tomato purée, 3 sliced garlic cloves, 3 thyme sprigs and 2 bay leaves. Deglaze with 500ml red wine, reduce slightly, then add enough beef stock (around 750ml-1L) to fully submerge the ribs. Return the ribs, cover and cook at 130°C for 4 hours until spoon tender. Remove the ribs, strain and remove the fat from the sauce (use a separator jug if you have one). Pass through a fine sieve and then reduce it until glossy and thick enough to coat the back of a spoon. Return the ribs to the sauce and baste. Silky mash. Sticky, rich beef. Absolute comfort food - elevated. #mash #shortrib #cooking #recipe #food

Toffee brown butter chocolate chip cookies!  RECIPE Toffee: - 1/2 cup unsalted butter - 1 cup light brown sugar - Pinch of salt  Cookie dough:  - 2 cups all purpose flour - 1 1/2 tsp salt - 1 tsp baking soda - 1 cup unsalted butter, melted - 2 tbsp room temp water - 1 cup dark brown sugar  - 1/2 cup white sugar - 1 tsp vanilla extract - 1/2 rounded tsp espresso powder  - 1 large egg - 1 egg yolk - 1 1/2 cups semi-sweet chocolate chunks - 1/2 dark chocolate chunks  - 1 cup toffee bits 1. Make the toffee: combine butter and brown sugar in a saucepan. Place over medium heat. Allow butter to melt and whisk together to combine with the sugar. Bring to a bubble, whisking consistently. Use a candy thermometer and wait for the mixture to reach 300F (about 8 minutes) then remove from heat and pour onto a silicone or parchment lined baking sheet. Quickly spread the mixture out with a spatula to an smooth slab. Let cool for 20 minutes until hardened. Break toffee apart into small pieces as desired.   2. For the cookies: Melt butter in a saucepan and cook over a medium heat until the milk solids have browned and the butter is a nutty brown color. Transfer to a Pyrex cup, and add the water to make the liquids equal to 1 cup. Allow to cool to room temperature, about 30 minutes.  3. In the meantime, in a small bowl mix together the flour, salt and baking soda. Set aside.  4. In a large bowl, combine the brown and white sugars with the brown butter, and whisk together vigorously to combine. Once homogenous, add the vanilla extract and espresso powder. Whisk to combine. Next, add the egg and egg yolk, whisk to combine.  5. Add the dry ingredients to the wet, and mix gently with a spatula to combine, stopping once you see no more streaks of flour and a dough has formed.  6. Add the chocolate and toffee bits and mix once more to combine.  7. Use a 3 tbsp cookie scoop to portion the cookie dough onto a lined plate or baking sheet. It should yield about 14 cookies. Cover and place in the freezer for at least 3 hours or overnight.  8. When ready to bake, preheat the oven to 350F and bake cookies for 15 minutes. Once golden brown, remove from oven. Transfer to a cooling rack after 5 minutes and sprinkle with flakey salt. For misshapen cookies, use a round cup or bowl to gently reform into a circle. Allow to cool and enjoy! Tips: I like using a high quality baking sheet like @williamsonoma’s gold touch series to make sure cookies bake evenly and don’t spread too thin! I’ve been making this base recipe for years, adapted from an old @buzzfeedtasty recipe, and think the addition of toffee has made my favorite iteration yet!

🥩 Oven-Roasted BBQ Brisket 🍖 This Oven-Roasted BBQ Brisket is slow-cooked until irresistibly tender, then finished with a rich, sticky barbecue glaze that caramelizes beautifully in the oven. Every slice is juicy, smoky, and packed with bold flavor, making it the perfect centerpiece for family dinners, weekend gatherings, or holiday meals. Ingredients For the Brisket • 4–5 lbs beef brisket, trimmed • 1 tbsp olive oil • 2 tsp smoked paprika • 2 tsp garlic powder • 2 tsp onion powder • 1½ tsp salt • 1 tsp black pepper • 1 tsp chili powder • ½ tsp ground cumin For the Roasting Base • 1 large onion, sliced • 4 cloves garlic, minced • 1 cup beef broth • 1 tbsp Worcestershire sauce For the BBQ Glaze • 1½ cups barbecue sauce, divided • 2 tbsp brown sugar • 1 tbsp apple cider vinegar Instructions 1. Preheat the oven to 300°F (150°C). Arrange the sliced onion and minced garlic in the bottom of a large roasting pan or Dutch oven. 2. Pat the brisket dry with paper towels, then rub it all over with olive oil. 3. In a small bowl, combine the smoked paprika, garlic powder, onion powder, salt, black pepper, chili powder, and cumin. Rub the seasoning mixture evenly over every side of the brisket. 4. Place the brisket fat-side up on top of the onions. Pour the beef broth and Worcestershire sauce around the meat. 5. Cover the pan tightly with a lid or heavy-duty aluminum foil and roast for 4½–5 hours, or until the brisket is fork-tender. 6. In a bowl, whisk together 1 cup of the barbecue sauce, brown sugar, and apple cider vinegar. 7. Remove the brisket from the oven and generously brush the top with the barbecue glaze. 8. Increase the oven temperature to 425°F (220°C). Return the brisket to the oven uncovered and roast for another 10–15 minutes, until the glaze becomes glossy, caramelized, and slightly charred around the edges. 9. Transfer the brisket to a cutting board and let it rest for 20 minutes before slicing thinly against the grain. 10. Drizzle the sliced brisket with the flavorful pan juices and serve with the remaining barbecue sauce. Serving Suggestions Serve with creamy mashed potatoes, baked beans, buttery cornbread, roasted corn on the cob, coleslaw, mac and cheese, or grilled vegetables for a classic Southern-style barbecue feast. Storage Store leftover brisket in an airtight container with a little extra barbecue sauce in the refrigerator for up to 4 days. Reheat gently in the oven or on the stovetop to keep the meat tender and juicy. Prep Time: 15 minutes Cook Time: 5 hours Total Time: 5 hours 35 minutes Servings: 8 Calories: Approximately 520 per serving #BBQBrisket #ComfortFood #EasyDinner #FamilyMeals #SlowRoasted

Apple Butter is a fall staple in our house and I’ve been making the same recipe for 4 years now. It’s even better than you can imagine, I promise. It’s packed with all the cozy fall flavors, thick, and so so good on a warm biscuit 🤤  Note: the original recipe by @MyBakingAddiction was made for 10-12 hours in a slow cooker, but I’ve adapted it for the stovetop!  INGREDIENTS • 6 ½ pounds apples, peeled, cored, and sliced • 1 cup granulated sugar • 1 cup brown sugar • 1 tablespoon ground cinnamon • ½ teaspoon ground nutmeg • ¼ teaspoon ground cloves • ¼ teaspoon salt • 1 tablespoon vanilla bean paste INSTRUCTIONS 1. Combine: Add apples, both sugars, cinnamon, nutmeg, cloves, salt, and vanilla bean paste to a large pot. Stir well to coat. 2. Cook: Simmer over low heat for 6–8 hours. Keep the lid on for the first half to trap heat and soften the apples, then remove the lid so excess liquid can evaporate. Stir often to prevent sticking. 3. Blend: Once the apples are deep brown, use an immersion blender (or stand blender in batches) and blend 7–10 minutes until ultra-smooth and velvety. 4. Thicken: Return to the stove and simmer uncovered for another 30 minutes to remove any last bit of moisture. 5. Store: Allow to cool, then spoon into jars. Makes about 4 pints. Keeps in the fridge up to 2 weeks or freezer up to 3 months. #applebutter #fallrecipes #fallbaking #food #applebutterrecipe

This is basically all the cozy, nostalgic flavors of a classic chicken pot pie, but turned into a creamy bowl of tiny pasta. We’ve got tender chicken, carrots, celery, peas, plenty of thyme, and a rich, savory broth that thickens as the pastina cooks until everything becomes silky, creamy, and almost pot pie filling-like. And because you simply cannot have chicken pot pie without the pie, little golden puff pastry “croutons” get piled right on top. They’re buttery, flaky, deeply golden, and honestly the part that brings the whole thing together. I finish them with a little Parmesan and fresh thyme while they’re still warm, then add them right before serving so they stay crisp against the creamy pastina underneath.
